newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-REDS SIGN MERCKER, THREE OTHER FREE AGENT PITCHERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-REDS SIGN MERCKER, THREE OTHER FREE AGENT PITCHERS.

text.p: The Cincinnati Reds, desperate to add arms to an unsettled rotation, signed left-hander Kent Mercker and three other free agent pitchers on Tuesday.

Mercker and right-hander Ricky Bones were signed to one-year contracts while righties David Nied and Rodney Bolton were inked to Triple-A deals and invited to spring training. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The 28-year-old Mercker was a combined 4-6 with a 6.98 ERA for Baltimore and Cleveland last season.

Mercker returns to the National League after pitching in parts of seven seasons with the Atlanta Braves. He was 9-4 with a 3.45 ERA in 1994 and threw a no-hitter against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Mercker was also part of a combined no-hitter in 1991.

Bones, 27, started the season in Milwaukee and was traded to the New York Yankees in August as part of a controversial deal involving Graeme Lloyd and Pat Listach. Bones was 7-14 with a 5.83 ERA in 32 games for the Brewers and appeared in four games for the Yankees, allowing 11 runs in seven innings.
Bones, a native of Puerto Rico, was 10-9 with a 3.43 ERA in 1994 and was named to the American League All-Star team.

Nied, 27, has spent the last four seasons in the Colorado organisation. He was the first pick in the 1992 expansion draft and started the Rockies' first game. Bothered by nagging injuries, Nied has a career record of 17-18 with a 5.06 ERA.
The 28-year-old Bolton spent the 1996 season in Japan after pitching in the Chicago White Sox organisation.
